paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: This figure compares the error rate (one average minus test accuracy), computation cost, and GPU memory across our approach and baselines, for fine-tuning Llama-3-8B on ten NLP tasks with QAdapter.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the GPU memory usage in gigabytes (GB) for different approaches employed in the fine-tuning of language models, specifically focusing on the QAdapter method. The vertical axis is labeled "GPU Memory (GB)" and ranges from 0 to 70, with tick marks indicating intervals of 10 GB. The horizontal axis lists the methods compared: "Full FT," "MTL-FT," "TAG," "Adapter," "QAdapter," and "Ours." Each approach is represented by a bar with distinct colors, where "Full FT," "MTL-FT," and "TAG" are depicted in orange and vary in height, with "Full FT" being the tallest at approximately 65 GB, "MTL-FT" at around 50 GB, and "TAG" somewhat lower. The "Adapter" and "QAdapter" bars are shorter, around 20 GB and 15 GB, respectively, both also in orange. Finally, the "Ours" bar, depicted in green, is noticeably the shortest at about 10 GB, which indicates a lower memory requirement compared to the other methods. The bars are presented in descending order based on GPU memory usage for the first three methods and do not have any additional visual enhancements or annotations.
